#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Brings up a ros2_control system (mock_components/GenericSystem) with two
# revolute joints (joint_a, joint_b), a joint_state_broadcaster, and a
# forward_command_controller/ForwardCommandController named
# position_controller that commands the position interface of both joints.
#
# Starts the controller_manager node in the background (detached) and then
# spawns the two controllers. Returns once both controllers are active.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash

LOG_DIR="$SCRIPT_DIR/log"
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"

ROBOT_DESCRIPTION="$(cat "$SCRIPT_DIR/robot.urdf")"

# Start the controller manager (ros2_control_node) in the background, fully
# detached from this shell so it keeps running after bringup.sh exits.
nohup ros2 run controller_manager ros2_control_node \
  --ros-args \
  -p "robot_description:=${ROBOT_DESCRIPTION}" \
  --params-file "$SCRIPT_DIR/controllers.yaml" \
  > "$LOG_DIR/controller_manager.log" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
disown

# Wait for the controller_manager services to come up before spawning
# controllers against it.
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
  if ros2 service list 2>/dev/null | grep -q "/controller_manager/list_controllers"; then
    break
  fi
  sleep 1
done

# Spawn (load, configure, activate) the controllers. The spawner processes
# exit on their own once the controller is active, so running them in the
# foreground here just waits until activation succeeds before this script
# returns.
ros2 run controller_manager spawner joint_state_broadcaster \
  --controller-manager /controller_manager \
  > "$LOG_DIR/spawner_joint_state_broadcaster.log" 2>&1

ros2 run controller_manager spawner position_controller \
  --controller-manager /controller_manager \
  > "$LOG_DIR/spawner_position_controller.log" 2>&1

echo "ros2_control bringup complete. Logs in $LOG_DIR"

# forward_command_controller/ForwardCommandController named
# position_controller that commands the position interface of both joints.
#
# Starts the controller_manager node in the background (detached) and then
# spawns the two controllers. Returns once both controllers are active.

set -eo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash

LOG_DIR="$SCRIPT_DIR/log"
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"

ROBOT_DESCRIPTION="$(cat "$SCRIPT_DIR/robot.urdf")"

# Start the controller manager (ros2_control_node) in the background, fully
# detached from this shell so it keeps running after bringup.sh exits.
nohup ros2 run controller_manager ros2_control_node \
  --ros-args \
  -p "robot_description:=${ROBOT_DESCRIPTION}" \
  --params-file "$SCRIPT_DIR/controllers.yaml" \
  > "$LOG_DIR/controller_manager.log" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
disown

# Wait for the controller_manager services to come up before spawning
# controllers against it.
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
  if ros2 service list 2>/dev/null | grep -q "/controller_manager/list_controllers"; then
    break
  fi
  sleep 1
done

# Spawn (load, configure, activate) the controllers. The spawner processes
# exit on their own once the controller is active, so running them in the
# foreground here just waits until activation succeeds before this script
# returns.
ros2 run controller_manager spawner joint_state_broadcaster \
  --controller-manager /controller_manager \
  > "$LOG_DIR/spawner_joint_state_broadcaster.log" 2>&1

ros2 run controller_manager spawner position_controller \
  --controller-manager /controller_manager \
  > "$LOG_DIR/spawner_position_controller.log" 2>&1

echo "ros2_control bringup complete. Logs in $LOG_DIR"
